name: ribbon
title: Ribbon plot
about: Shows how the selected clusters change over time: per cluster and sample group, a mean line inside a band from the lowest to the highest feature.

shows.panel: cluster; every cluster is drawn and the unselected ones are faded, or only the selected ones when expanded
shows.facet: sample group, stacked inside the panel on a shared time axis
shows.line: mean of the features at each timepoint
shows.band: lowest to highest feature at each timepoint
shows.colour: one line and band per colour group: level 1 (default), level 2, type, or none
shows.y axis: shared by the sample groups of a cluster, separate for each cluster

reads.selectedClusters: which panels are highlighted (or shown, when expanded)
reads.level1: line and band are computed from the passing features only (when the scope is filtered); also the colour groups by default
reads.level2: line and band are computed from the passing features only (when the scope is filtered); the colour groups when chosen
reads.scope: filtered features, or every feature of the cluster
reads.ribbonExpand: all clusters with the unselected faded, or only the selected ones, larger

features.name: shape
features.how: course of the mean line: even, increase, decrease, hump, dip, multi-peak or mixed

features.name: peak
features.how: timepoint of the highest mean; early, mid or late by its position on the time axis

features.name: fitted_shape
features.how: the simple function (line, U / n, L / J, peak / valley, step) that fits the mean line best

features.name: band_width
features.how: highest minus lowest feature at each timepoint; summarised as mean width, largest width or area

features.name: width_trend
features.how: whether the band gets wider or narrower over time

features.name: colour_divergence
features.how: gap between the mean lines of the colour groups of one cluster

features.name: comparison
features.how: relation of two mean curves (two sample groups, two time windows or two clusters), judged on their fitted functions

features.name: similarity
features.how: two clusters are similar in a sample group when the Pearson r of their fitted functions is high enough, or both are flat; with several sample groups the question must say in all of them or in any

target.pattern: increase, decrease, peak, opposite shape, similar shape to another cluster, colour lines disagree
target.ribbon: tight / wide ribbon, features follow the same trajectory

descriptor.pattern:
"what is its pattern", "do they decline", "how do their shapes relate", "at which time point
  does each cluster peak".
